record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Function Field Arithmetic — The Influence of John Tate’s Work
record.original_question: What are the complete algebraic relations among the multizeta values ζ(s1, …, sk) over A = Fq[t], where these multizeta values are defined by summing 1/(n1^s1 ··· nk^sk) over monic polynomials n1, …, nk in A with strictly decreasing degrees? In particular, which relations replace the classical sum-shuffle and integral-shuffle relations in positive characteristic, and how should the additional digit-phenomena constraints be formulated?

evidence.quote: The relations satisfied by them are under investigation. These relations are not quite the classical sum-shuffle and integral-shuffle relations and involve subtle ‘digit phenomena’.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power, $A=\mathbb{F}_q[t]$, $K=\mathbb{F}_q(t)$, and let $K_\infty=\mathbb{F}_q((1/t))$ denote the completion at the place at infinity. For a positive integer $s$ and a non-negative integer $d$, set
$$ S_d(s) \;=\; \sum_{\substack{n\in A\text{ monic} \\ \deg n = d}} \frac{1}{n^s} \;\in\; K. $$
For positive integers $s_1,\dots,s_k$ define the function-field multizeta value
$$ \zeta_A(s_1,\dots,s_k) \;=\; \sum_{d_1 > d_2 > \cdots > d_k \ge 0} S_{d_1}(s_1)\,S_{d_2}(s_2)\cdots S_{d_k}(s_k) \;=\; \sum \frac{1}{n_1^{s_1}\cdots n_k^{s_k}} \;\in\; K_\infty, $$
the second sum running over $k$-tuples of monic polynomials $n_i\in A$ with $\deg n_1 > \deg n_2 > \cdots > \deg n_k \ge 0$. The integer $k$ is called the depth and $s_1+\cdots+s_k$ the weight.

Problem. Determine all $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear (equivalently, all polynomial) algebraic relations among the values $\zeta_A(s_1,\dots,s_k)$, $k\ge 1$, $s_i\ge 1$. Specifically:

(a) Identify a complete family of "shuffle-type" identities that, in positive characteristic, replace the classical sum-shuffle and integral-shuffle product formulas; that is, for any positive integers $r_1,\dots,r_a$ and $u_1,\dots,u_b$, express
$$ \zeta_A(r_1,\dots,r_a)\cdot \zeta_A(u_1,\dots,u_b) $$
as an explicit $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear combination of multizeta values of the same weight $r_1+\cdots+r_a+u_1+\cdots+u_b$, and prove that the resulting set of identities generates the full ideal of relations.

(b) Formulate and prove the additional "digit-phenomena" identities (relations forced by carries/digit interactions in base $q$ arising from the power sums $S_d(s)$) that are not consequences of the shuffle-type identities in (a).

(c) Show that the relations in (a) and (b) together generate all $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebraic relations among the $\zeta_A(s_1,\dots,s_k)$, and deduce the dimension of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space spanned by multizeta values of each fixed weight $w$.
artifact.status_search_result: Major progress has been made: Thakur established shuffle-type product relations for multizeta values over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$ with $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficients, making their span an algebra, and Chen and others gave a $t$-motivic interpretation. Conjectural dimensions (Todd's conjecture) and many explicit relations including digit-phenomena identities have been proved. However, a complete description of all algebraic relations (and a full proof that shuffle plus digit-phenomena identities generate the entire ideal of relations, with proved dimension formulas in every weight) is still considered an open program.

status_evidence.title: Multizeta values for function fields: A survey (Thakur)
status_evidence.snippet: Despite the failure of naive analogs of sum/integral shuffle relations, Thakur proved shuffle relations making the Fp-span into an algebra; complete relations under investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Shuffle relations established; full set of relations still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: A t-motivic interpretation of shuffle relations for multizeta values
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a t-motivic interpretation of Thakur's shuffle relations for function-field multizeta values.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural understanding via t-motives; problem of all relations remains.

status_evidence.title: Shuffle Relations for Function Field Multizeta Values
status_evidence.snippet: Thakur shows multizeta values satisfy shuffle relations with Fp-coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes partial answer (shuffle-type relations) for the relation problem.
